page.title: Settings
page.purpose: Expose the configuration that governs how much of a personal device this scenario may see and retain — redaction policy, retention, consumer grants, and the bridge connection.

priorities.statement: The redaction policy in force, and what it does not cover, are stated before any other setting.
priorities.notes: This is the setting that decides whether a personal device's screen can end up in a shared evidence store. It outranks connection details.

priorities.statement: Which consumers may hold a lease is shown as an explicit list, never implied by a global toggle.
priorities.notes: A capability that can drive a personal phone deserves credential-grade treatment, which means named grants rather than on/off.

priorities.statement: Retention for captures is shown with what pins a run beyond it.
priorities.notes: Release-referenced runs are exempt from expiry; an operator who does not know that will believe captures are gone when they are not.

states.description: Settings loaded with a redaction policy in force and at least one consumer grant.
Configuration is being fetched; no policy is asserted yet.
No redaction policy has been defined and no consumer has been granted. Stated as an unsafe default rather than a neutral blank form.
A redaction policy exists but does not cover every capture kind; the uncovered kinds are named.
The bridge connection was last confirmed longer ago than the health interval; shown as unconfirmed rather than connected.
Configuration could not be loaded. No policy is presented as in force while its actual value is unknown.
A submitted setting was rejected; the field and the reason are named and the prior value remains in force.

elements.name: Redaction
elements.description: The policy applied to captures before they leave the producer, and which capture kinds it covers.
Names capture kinds the current policy does not cover, including the case where no policy exists at all.

elements.name: Consumer grants
elements.description: Which consumers may acquire a lease, scoped by device and verb class.

elements.name: Retention
elements.description: How long captures, audit, and run records are kept, and what pins a run past expiry.
Reach-plane connection status and when it was last confirmed.

elements.name: Revoke
elements.description: Removes a consumer's ability to acquire new leases.

claims.statement: The redaction policy reads before connection and retention configuration.
claims.rationale: Priority 1. This is the setting with the highest consequence on the page, and settings pages default to ordering by system layer rather than by risk.

claims.statement: When no redaction policy is defined, the page states that captures are unprotected rather than presenting a neutral empty form.
claims.rationale: SECURITY.md records the undefined redaction policy as a high-severity gap. A blank form communicates 'nothing configured yet'; the truth is 'nothing is protecting these frames'.

claims.statement: Capture kinds not covered by the current redaction policy are named individually.
claims.rationale: A partially applied policy reads as full protection unless the uncovered kinds are enumerated — device logs and clipboard are the likely omissions.

claims.statement: Consumers permitted to hold a lease are presented as an enumerable list with their scope.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. A global enable toggle cannot express per-device or per-verb scope, and SECURITY.md flags all-or-nothing granting as a medium gap.

claims.statement: Each grant can be revoked from the keyboard.
claims.rationale: Revocation is the control an operator reaches for under time pressure; it should not depend on a pointer.

claims.statement: Retention shows both the expiry window and what exempts a run from it.
claims.rationale: Priority 3. DATA.md pins release-referenced runs; an operator who does not know that will believe captures are deleted when they are retained.

claims.statement: A bridge connection not confirmed within the health interval is perceivably different from a confirmed one.
claims.rationale: Consistent with D-002 at the connection scale: last-known-good is not the same claim as currently-reachable.

claims.statement: A rejected setting names the field and reason, and the previously effective value remains stated.
claims.rationale: Leaving a rejected form in an ambiguous state is how an operator comes to believe a policy is in force when it is not.
